title: Prove sharp quarter-dimension repair for two Gaussian banks (no κ)
body:
## Summary

A scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. One Walsh/Gaussian transform on N=2^t addresses, t>=2, cannot become two balanced independent coordinate banks with ordinary correction rank below N/4. The bound is sharp, even with unitary normalized targets.

```text
free row/column partitions + free invertible monomial adapters
    one Gaussian transform + linear correction
    -> correction rank >= N/4
    -> N/4 commuting rank-one reflections attain equality
```

Both independent bank targets may be chosen freely. The proof gives the exact attaining targets; they are not two preassigned native jobs. Ordinary address rank is not recursive frame rank, a native ADD count or a physical tariff. No new kappa or selected-frontier change follows.

This is an original pooling-interface question aimed at the complex supplier bottleneck. Greer Guthrie's [PR679](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/679) monomial-support/volume warning is credited context. The submatrix rank inequality is classical, associated with [Lokam's spectral method](https://doi.org/10.1006/jcss.2001.1786). Walsh orthogonality, Householder reflections, tensor products and rank telescoping retain their usual credit. No literature-priority claim is made. The package credits the reciprocal and clean-encoding predecessors and retained Gaussian/native authors.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19373319). The delivered scope matches the claim.

## Evidence

Before this result, the cited monomial support warning excludes correction rank zero. The new balanced-coordinate contract has the sharp N/4 lower bound and an exact all-t reflection construction.

- All 4,940 balanced row/column subset pairs at N=2,4,8 pass rational elimination, separate F101 elimination and the classical rank inequality. At N=8 the exact rank histogram is 84 / 1,344 / 3,472 at ranks 2 / 3 / 4.
- Five complete sharp operators at N=4,8,16,32,64 have correction ranks 1,2,4,8,16. A literal sequence of fiber reflections equals a separately constructed target. Full rank, orthogonality, involutivity and both zero cross-blocks pass.
- All 5,456 raw Gaussian tensor entries match the independent monomial formula. Fifteen omitted-reflection controls, five invalid inputs, the rank-zero counterexample and the two-address boundary pass.
- CPython 3.12.15 warning-strict direct checks pass normally and with -O, each locally timed at 0.92 seconds. Both registered commands pass in 2.05 seconds total. Normal/optimized generated receipts are identical and hash all seven package files.
- Committed-byte/mode and source-history checks pass at d5c789b7927781143152d11381fef3c21e68a7a5. Official export integrity passes; an optimized read-only Git-free replay with empty PATH produces the identical receipt. Selected baseline bindings pass as metadata orientation only. AST and whitespace checks pass.

Reproduce from the repository root using the actual local interpreter:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/balanced-walsh-pooling/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/balanced-walsh-pooling/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/balanced-walsh-pooling
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/balanced-walsh-pooling --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 path can replace that path. Expected direct marker: PASS_BALANCED_WALSH_POOLING. Standard library only; no predecessor scientific suite or receipt is imported or replayed. The universal statement rests on PROOF.md.

## Limitations

General encoders mixing across banks, nonlinear repairs, and fixed-target optimality are outside this result. Causal collection/scatter, signed native realization, ownership, arbitrary dirty restoration, precision, stock, tape, compiler and complete paid/productive invoice remain unpriced. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No selected cold replay, native/compiler build, Lean or Docker was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Pin one actual chronological pair of desired native jobs and compute its full required correction before pricing collection, delivery and dirty restoration.
- Specify a paid cross-bank encoder and its inverse, then test a complete changed producer/consumer contract and signed moment. The present coordinate obstruction does not cover such an encoder.

No follow-on scope is reserved.

## Related open work

- [PR6443](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6443) optimizes correction rank for specified repeated Clifford lanes under a unitary reciprocal encoder. This result instead allows independent coordinate partitions, monomial endpoints and freely chosen bank targets; its numerical optimum is for a different contract.
- [PR6442](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6442) prices rank-one repairs of a weighted interchange wrapper. Its word and endpoint differ from this Gaussian bank-separation problem; rank telescoping is a classical shared method.
- [PR6399](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6399) fuses two serial donor transports with a restored scratch correction. It does not replace independent banks by one pooled transform.
- [PR6529](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6529) fuses scaled serial transport intervals and prices their whole caller. This package gives an algebraic obstruction under a different boundary and makes no comparison of kappa or paid profiles.

Targeted main/merged/general-form searches, current PRs, recent claims and reservations were checked before commitment. Arbitrary historical diffs, sparse notes, unpublished work and non-atomic changes remain coverage limits. No extra computations audited other contributions.
